title: Better Auth accent-insensitive email lookup can reset another account
summary: With an accent-insensitive database collation, a password-reset lookup may return an account whose stored email differs from the requested address only by accent marks. The reset code is sent to the requested address instead of the stored account address, allowing someone who receives mail at the accent variant to reset the victim account without victim action. The advisory describes three defects but attributes only this accent-insensitive lookup to the scanner; this row represents only that one finding.
ai_role: The accented-address issue was discovered by Anthropic’s OSS Scanner, ANT-2026-Y7X5RTID. The other defects in the combined advisory are not included in this case.
classification_note: The vulnerability is documented as a public disclosure; the source does not establish prior defender knowledge or exploitation.
remediation_note: Upgrade better-auth to 1.7.16 or 1.8.0-beta.5. The fix requires the stored account email to match the requested address ignoring case and sends reset mail to the account’s stored address.

impacts.conditions: emailOTP() is used with a database collation that ignores accents; attacker can receive mail at an accent-variant address.
